title: The teacher takes command
hook: Duryodhana asks his new commander for one thing: bring Yudhishthira to me alive
carry: acharya devo bhava: honor the teacher as god
tomorrow: Arjuna's far away. who can break Drona's wheel?

segments.voice: Yesterday Bhishma asked for a pillow of arrows, and from that bed came the thousand names of Vishnu. Your line: the thousand names came from a bed of arrows. Now the Kauravas need a new commander.

A teacher takes command of an army sent against his own students. Bhishma lies on the field, and the man the Kauravas choose to lead them is Drona, the master of arms who trained both sets of cousins as boys, who once tested the princes with a toy bird in a treetop and found that only Arjuna saw nothing but its head. Duryodhana honors him, and Drona, pleased, offers him a gift: ask for whatever you want. Duryodhana's answer surprises him. Not Arjuna's death. Not victory. Bring me Yudhishthira, he says. Alive.
screen: `THE TEACHER TAKES COMMAND.` → `TEACHER OF BOTH SETS OF COUSINS.` → `BRING ME YUDHISHTHIRA ALIVE.`

segments.voice: Drona is glad to hear it, at first. In Ganguli's telling, he praises Duryodhana: you don't want your cousin killed, so maybe you mean to make peace. But Duryodhana's reasons show. A captured Yudhishthira could be drawn into the dice again, and the Pandavas sent back to the forest. Same game, second round. Drona agrees, with one condition: only if Arjuna isn't beside him. So a band of Trigarta warriors swears an oath to challenge Arjuna and never come back until he's dead or they are: the samshaptakas, the sworn ones. Arjuna won't refuse a challenge, and he rides away. Now step back, because this part of the story asks something hard. Hindus hold the teacher, the guru or acharya, almost as high as God. The Taittiriya Upanishad tells a student leaving school: treat your mother as a god, your father as a god, your teacher as a god. Acharya devo bhava. That's why, on the war's first morning, Yudhishthira walked unarmed to Drona, bowed to him and asked his blessing. Drona gave it, and told him plainly that he was bound to the Kaurava side by what they had given him. So the epic holds both: the teacher is sacred, and a teacher can still stand on the wrong side. Arjuna will honor Drona and fight him. In the coming days, that empty space where Arjuna should be will matter.
screen: `THE DICE AGAIN` · `THE SWORN ONES` · `TREAT YOUR TEACHER AS A GOD` · then, large: `ACHARYA DEVO BHAVA`

segments.voice: Fold your hands at your chest. Many Hindu children learn a verse that begins Gurur Brahma, Gurur Vishnu: the teacher is Brahma, the teacher is Vishnu. Bring to mind one teacher who shaped you, in a classroom, a kitchen, a gym. Breathing in, see their face. Breathing out, bow your head a little toward them, the way Yudhishthira bowed to Drona with armies watching. If you pray, thank God for them. If you don't, simply thank them in your mind.
Drona. The teacher of the Kauravas and the Pandavas, now commanding the Kaurava army against his own students.
Your line: acharya devo bhava: honor the teacher as god. Even when the teacher rides against you. That's day eight hundred thirty-one.

screen: `DAY 831 COUNTS.` → `TOMORROW: ARJUNA'S FAR AWAY. WHO CAN BREAK DRONA'S WHEEL?`

howItsDone: Hindus honor teachers on Guru Purnima, and many students touch a teacher's feet before a lesson, an exam or a performance; Drona is remembered as the guru of both the Kauravas and the Pandavas.
